channel.title: ShopNow Kitchen guides
channel.description: Kitchen gear, explained like a friend would. Every claim traced to its source.

item.title: Air fryer chicken breast: how do you know it is done?
item.description: Cooking chicken breast in an air fryer: the safe internal temperature, where to place the probe, why colour and texture mislead, and which tracked appliance suits which job.

item.title: Air fryer presets: how many do you actually need?
item.description: Preset counts are a marketing number. What matters is how many presets match the food you already cook, and how the tracked appliances differ on this.

item.title: How to read an Amazon listing before you buy a kitchen appliance
item.description: A practical method for checking a marketplace listing against the manufacturer's own page: model numbers, temperature ranges, wattage, dimensions and certification claims, with a worked example from our own shelf.

item.title: Air fryer, toaster oven or microwave: which earns the space?
item.description: Air fryer, toaster oven and microwave each solve a different problem. How to work out which one you actually need, what each shape costs you, and what to give up if you pick it.

item.title: Is your meat thermometer telling you the right number?
item.description: How to use a meat thermometer so the reading means something: USDA target temperatures, probe placement, calibration checks, and what wireless specs like range and probe count really buy you.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: A buyer's interrogation guide for combination air fryers, toaster ovens and other multi-function appliances: counting real functions, presets, accessories and the learning curve.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: A practical method for weighing dishwasher claims, hand-washing reality, counter footprint, ventilation clearance and open-door space before you buy a kitchen appliance.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: What quart ratings measure, what they leave out, and a printable checklist of questions to compare air fryer capacity without the marketing gloss.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: A plain-English comparison of basket-style and oven-style air fryers: what each shape does well, what to check before you choose, and how the appliances we track blur the line.

item.title: Instant-read or leave-in probe: which one do you need?
item.description: Instant-read and leave-in wireless thermometers do completely different jobs. How to choose between them, what their published specifications actually promise, and where the numbers come from.

item.title: How much counter space does an air fryer really need?
item.description: Counter space is the constraint that decides most kitchen purchases. How to measure it properly, what to add for an open drawer and a swinging door, and the real footprints of the three countertop appliances we track.

item.title: Holiday hosting on a small counter: a plan for the big meal
item.description: A seasonal plan for cooking a big meal on limited counter space: what to cook where, the counter space each appliance needs, and the temperatures to aim for.

item.title: Is a Black Friday air fryer deal worth waiting for?
item.description: Judging a Black Friday air fryer offer without a price history: match the model string, read the capacity, and know what an affiliate page may show.

item.title: Dual basket or single basket: which one for four people?
item.description: Dual-basket and single-basket air fryers trade against each other in ways the product pages do not spell out: batch size, cooking time, cleanup and counter footprint, for a household of four.

item.title: Can you cook a whole chicken in it? Check the sheet first
item.description: Whether a whole chicken fits, worked out from the capacity and case size makers publish, plus the USDA poultry temperature that decides doneness.
